title: Two-term constant-sheaf resolution of Z/ell^N and its tensor augmentation
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $N\geq1$, and $\mathcal C$ a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_{\mathcal C}$ and $Q=(\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ be constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with the coefficient rings of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], and total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The complex $C=[R\xrightarrow{\ell^N}R]$, in degrees $-1,0$, has flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and its degree-zero quotient augmentation $\epsilon:C\to Q[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For any $R$-module sheaf $L$ such that multiplication by $\ell^N$ is injective, the canonical augmentation
$$\operatorname{Tot}(L[0]\otimes_R C)\longrightarrow(L\otimes_R Q)[0]$$
is a quasi-isomorphism. Here the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] canonically identifies $L\otimes_R Q$ with $L/\ell^NL$, by $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto a[x]$.

proof.text: Put A = Z_l, B = Z/l^n and t = l^n. Mathlib PadicInt.ker_toZModPow identifies the kernel of the reduction homomorphism with the principal ideal (t). PadicInt is a domain, so multiplication by t is injective; ZMod.ringHom_surjective makes the quotient map surjective. Lift these maps by ULift, obtaining a short exact sequence of A-modules. The constant-presheaf functor preserves finite limits and colimits, as witnessed by its evaluation functors, and module sheafification preserves both. Its additive structure identifies the image of multiplication by t with t times the identity. Therefore the specified constant-module sequence is short exact, by [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact; Mathlib PadicInt.ker_toZModPow and ZMod.ringHom_surjective for the coefficient calculation

proof.text: Construct the canonical freeModule-to-unit map by the module-sheafification adjunction, induced by the constant-ring sheafification unit. Its underlying map is locally bijective, hence an isomorphism, and on constant sections it is the ring sheafification unit. The tensor unitor makes tensoring with this free module exact; tensoring with a zero module is zero. Thus the complex double(t), supported in degrees -1 and 0, has site-flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. It is strictly bounded above by zero, so [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] supplies exactly its independent-coefficient K-flatness.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; tensor unit as in sites-modules.tex Section 03EK

proof.text: Set $\epsilon^0=q$ and $\epsilon^i=0$ for $i\ne0$. The relation $qt=0$ makes this a cochain map. The cohomology formula of [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] and Step 1 give $H^{-1}(C)=\ker(t:R\to R)=0$, $H^0(C)=\operatorname{coker}(t:R\to R)\cong Q$, and zero in every other degree. The degree-zero cohomology map of $\epsilon$ is exactly this cokernel identification, since it is induced by $q$. All other cohomology maps are between zero sheaves. Hence $\epsilon:C\to Q[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

source.place: Tag 0115, definition-quasi-isomorphism-cochain; elementary two-term cohomology calculation

proof.text: For every L, the tensorLeft L functor preserves coefficient-sized colimits and is additive by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. Apply it to the quotient cokernel. The canonical free-module unitor carries tensorLeft L applied to multiplication by t to multiplication by t on L. Uniqueness of colimits and cokernel.mapIso yield the isomorphism L tensor Q = coker(t on L). Compare the explicit site tensor to the monoidal tensor using their sheafification presentations. Naturality of the comparison, the sheafification unit, and the unitor gives precisely the stated formula x tensor q(a) maps to a[x]. No injectivity on L is used.

source.place: Tag 03EP, lemma-tensor-commute-colimits, item (2); Section 03EK tensor unit and the cokernel universal property

proof.text: The mapBifunctorSingle₁Iso comparison identifies the signed total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] with tensorLeft L applied degreewise to double(t); the second differential has sign +1. Apply the functor to the coefficient augmentation and use the single-complex comparison. The mapped quotient sequence remains exact at its middle and right end by preservation of cokernels. When t on L is mono, the mapped degree -1 differential is mono by the free-module unitor. The short-complex criteria therefore show that the induced augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Finally the explicit component formula for mapBifunctorSingle₁Iso and naturality of the tensor comparison prove the required zero-summand normalization.

lean.statement: theorem constant_two_term_resolution (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : ∃ (K : CochainComplex (Modules J l) ℤ) (em : K.X (-1) ≅ freeModule J l) (e0 : K.X 0 ≅ freeModule J l), (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 → IsZero (K.X i)) ∧ K.d (-1) 0 = em.hom ≫ ((l ^ n) • 𝟙 (freeModule J l)) ≫ e0.inv ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := (constantSheaf J CommRingCat.{u}).obj (CommRingCat.of (Coeff.{u} l))) (K.X i)) ∧ CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients K ∧ (∃ ε : K ⟶ single J l (quotientSheaf J l n), ε.f 0 ≫ (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0 _).hom = e0.hom ≫ quotientMap J l n ∧ QuasiIso ε) ∧ (∀ L : Modules J l, ∃ φ : (siteSheafTensorRight (quotientSheaf J l n)).obj L ≅ cokernel ((l ^ n) • 𝟙 L), (∀ (U : Sᵒᵖ) (x : L.val.obj U) (a : Coeff.{u} l), φ.hom.val.app U (siteSheafTensorTmul L (quotientSheaf J l n) U x ((quotientMap J l n).val.app U (constantSection J l U a))) = (cokernel.π ((l ^ n) • 𝟙 L)).val.app U (((constantCoefficientUnit J (Coeff.{u} l)).app U a) • x)) ∧ (Mono ((l ^ n) • 𝟙 L) → ∃ α : total J l L K ⟶ single J l ((siteSheafTensorRight (quotientSheaf J l n)).obj L), zeroSummand J l L K ≫ α.f 0 ≫ (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0 _).hom = (siteSheafTensorRight (K.X 0)).map (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0 L).hom ≫ siteSheafTensorSecondMap L (e0.hom ≫ quotientMap J l n) ∧ QuasiIso α))
lean.note: Uses the recorded constantCoefficientModule functor for the actual constant coefficient and quotient sheaves. Helpers expose the lifted quotient map, sheafification-unit sections, signed total tensor, and canonical (0,0)-summand. Both augmentations are normalized by equations; the quotient identification is specified on local pure tensors and does not assume injectivity. The added, already recorded constant-coefficient definition node supplies precisely this constant-module interface.
